newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares down as cement firm privatises.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares down as cement firm privatises.

text.p: The Egyptian stock exchange back-pedalled for the first time on Monday since the all-share index last week broke record highs.
But brokers attributed the recession to a fall in the share price of privatised Helwan Portland Cement and not to a market correction for shares across the board.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index receded slightly by 0.12 points to 276.05 points on Monday.
It was the index's first reversal since its steady climb to record highs when it broke last week the previous record of 255.05 points set in October 1994.
Turnover was bloated to 346.7 million pounds ($101.9 million) by the listing of Helwan Portland Cement shares as part of the Egyptian government's privatisation programme.
"The market was a bit slow today. The main activity was Helwan Cement," said broker Elwy Taymour of EFG-Hermes.
"The price of Helwan shares went down. It was a large volume. I think it's just because of Helwan that the index fall took place, said broker Omar Ramzy of Delta EAB.
The CMA said 5.26 million Helwan shares were sold, worth 308 million pounds. Shares closed down 12 percent at 57.50 pounds.

Helwan Cement increased net profits for financial year 1995/96 to 125.52 million pounds ($36.9 million) from 103.61 million a year earlier. The year ended on June 30. Net profits in the first quarter of 96/97 were 35 million pounds.

The firm, one of Egypt's leading cement manufacturers, had said it was raising dividends for 1995/96 to five pounds from the 4.75 pounds it had promised investors earlier this year. Dividends for 1994/95 were four pounds per share.
Suez Cement shares slipped 0.25 pounds closing at 56.61 pounds in the day's second highest turnover of 5.86 million pounds.
In addition to cement, the milling sector continued to dominate turnover but there was some profit-taking.
"Some of the milling shares went down, I think because of the profit-taking. It was really quiet and focused on Helwan," said Taymour.

Upper Egypt Flour Mill saw turnover of 2.2 million pounds but closed down also 1.25 pounds to 73.00. Shares of Central and West Delta Flour Mills, which announced a profit rise on Monday of 43.121 million pounds in financial year 1995/96, fell 2 pounds to 88 pounds in turnover of 2.2 million.
Amriyah Cement was the day's fifth highest taker in terms of turnover, with 2.18 million pounds changing hands. Its share closed at 65.00 pounds.
General Silos and Storage was one of the day's top ten shares in terms of turnover. Of that group its shares rose the most, by 3.85 pounds to close at 56.15.
Of a total 59 stocks traded, 21 rose, 19 fell and the rest closed unchanged.
The CMA index for openly traded firms rose to 432.8 points from Sunday's 430.6 points and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms fell to 189.37 points from 190.1.
$1 = 3.4 pounds
